title: A Job at a Café
description: Four recordings about getting and starting a job at a café: an interview, a phone message, two colleagues and a welcome talk.
instructions: Read the questions for each part first. Then press Play and listen. Choose the best answer (A, B or C) for each question.

parts.title: Part 1 · The interview
parts.intro: You will hear Mrs Taylor interviewing Duc for a job at her café.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Come in, Duc, and take a seat. Thank you for coming. Have you worked in a café before?

script.speaker: Duc
script.text: No, not in a café. But I worked in my uncle's shop last summer, so I'm used to talking to customers.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: That's useful. Now, we need someone for weekends. Can you work on Saturdays and Sundays?

script.speaker: Duc
script.text: Saturdays are fine. On Sundays, I play football in the morning, but I can start at one o'clock.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: That's OK. Saturday is from nine to five, and Sunday is from one to six. We pay seven pounds an hour.

script.speaker: Duc
script.text: That's good. Do I need to wear a uniform?

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Yes, we give you a green apron and a hat, but you should bring black trousers and comfortable shoes.

script.speaker: Duc
script.text: No problem. Can I ask one more thing? Is it a busy place?

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Very busy at lunchtime, because the office workers come in. But it's quiet in the afternoon, so you can learn slowly.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Well, you seem very friendly. Can you start next Saturday?

parts.title: Part 2 · A phone message
parts.intro: You will hear a voicemail message from the café owner to a new worker.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Hello, Linh. This is Tom from the café. I just wanted to tell you about your first day.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Please come at half past eight, not nine. We open at nine, and I want to show you around first.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Come to the back door, not the front. It's in the little street next to the bank. Ring the bell, and I'll let you in.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: You will work with Jack for the first two days. He is very kind, and he knows everything about the machines.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: Don't worry about lunch. We give all our workers a free sandwich and a drink.

script.speaker: Tom
script.text: If you are ill or you can't come, please phone me before eight o'clock. See you on Monday. Bye!

parts.title: Part 3 · Learning the job
parts.intro: You will hear Jack showing Linh how things work in the café.

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: OK, Linh, this is the coffee machine. It looks difficult, but it is easy. Press the green button first.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: And what is the red button for?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: That's for hot milk. Be careful, because it gets very hot. I burned my hand on my first day.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Oh no! I'll be careful. How much is a large coffee?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: A large coffee is three pounds twenty. A small one is two pounds fifty. Tea is cheaper, only two pounds.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: And do we take cards?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: Yes, but not for small things. If someone buys only a tea, we ask for cash.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: I see. What about the cakes? Do they bake them here?

script.speaker: Jack
script.text: No, Mrs Taylor's sister makes them at home. The lemon cake is the most popular, but she sometimes runs out by noon.

script.speaker: Linh
script.text: Great. Now, I'll take the order from table four. Wish me luck!

parts.title: Part 4 · A welcome talk
parts.intro: You will hear Mrs Taylor giving a talk to the café workers.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to our team. I want to tell you three important things about working here.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: First, always smile at the customers. A friendly face makes people come back. Even when you are tired, try to look happy.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Second, keep the café clean. Wash your hands often, and clean the tables as soon as a customer leaves. A dirty table is a big problem.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Third, please don't use your phone while you are working. If you must make a call, go outside. I'm not angry about this, but customers don't like it.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Finally, I have some good news. Next month, we are going to open a small garden at the back. We will need more workers, so tell your friends.

script.speaker: Mrs Taylor
script.text: Thank you for listening. Now, let's open the doors!
